title: Points as tuples
description:
Work with points stored as `(x, y)` tuples:

```python
def parse_point(text): ...          # "3,4" or " 3 , -4 " -> (3, 4) / (3, -4) as ints
def distance(p, q): ...             # straight-line distance between two points
def closest(points, target): ...    # the point nearest to target (the first one on a tie); None for no points
def bounds(points): ...             # ((min_x, min_y), (max_x, max_y)) of all points
```
hints: Each `def` is a small function: it receives values in its brackets and hands a result back with `return`, which can be a tuple: `return (x, y)`. Lesson 3.01 covers functions in full.
`int(" 3 ")` already ignores the spaces around the number, so splitting on the comma is enough.
Unpack tuples straight in the parameters' first line: `(x1, y1), (x2, y2) = p, q`.
For `bounds`, collect all the x values in one list and all the y values in another, then use `min` and `max` on each.
